1	# Registries — the model and the group cache
2	
3	> DevDesk architecture notes. Referenced from `.claude/CLAUDE.md`;
4	> read this file when working on the code it describes.
5	
6	## Registry model
7	
8	`RegistryConfig.Registries` is one flat list holding both plain registries and
9	repository-manager groups, told apart by `kind` (§3.8). A group fronts several
10	registries and is pullable itself, which is why they share a list.
11	
12	| Field | Meaning |
13	|---|---|
14	| `slug` | DevDesk's own identifier: what `parent` points at and what the group cache is keyed on. Everything Docker-facing stays keyed on `url`, because Docker is. |
15	| `kind` | `registry` or `group` |
16	| `parent` | slug of the owning group — carried by discovered members, not normally by config entries |
17	| `provider` | `generic`, `nexus`, `harbor`, `artifactory`, `gitlab`; declared, never sniffed from the URL |
18	| `auth_mode` | `credentials`, `anonymous`, or `inherit` for a member. Replaces `auth_enabled`, which is migrated at load and then dropped. |
19	| `repo_prefix` | what goes in front of the repository name. With `url` it is the entry's **address** (§3.18) |
20	
21	**An entry is an address, not a URL** (§3.18, D39). The pair `(url, repo_prefix)`
22	is what a registry is reached by, and both directions derive from it — the browse
23	asks `<url>/v2/<prefix>/<repo>/tags/list` (through `oci.ListRegistryTags`, the one tag lister, which follows `Link` pagination), the pull reference is
24	`<url>/<prefix>/<repo>:<tag>` — so they cannot mean two different repositories.
25	That disagreement is exactly what D39 was: `NexusDetector` synthesised a member
26	as `host/repository/<name>`, which browses (200) and cannot pull (404), because
27	the Docker client puts `/v2/` first and the whole path after it.
28	
29	Like `provider`, it is **declared, never sniffed**. Whether a repository answers
30	on a path prefix, a connector port or a subdomain is a setting on that repository
31	(`docker.httpPort`, `docker.httpsPort`, `docker.subdomain`), and the one endpoint
32	carrying it answers 403 to an ordinary pull account — the same endpoint that
33	would say what a group's members are. An instance that refuses one refuses both,
34	so guessing is not a fallback, it is the defect.
35	
36	The same declaration drives the image search header (DEVDESK-308): a
37	`provider: nexus` + `kind: group` entry, its discovered members, and a declared
38	entry with `parent: <slug>` pointing at such a group are listed from cached
39	content only, so the browser's level 1 header shows them on a `Cached only`
40	line. The provider is read from the config (`config.IsNexusGroup`), never
41	guessed from the URL. See `network.md`, "Level 1 header summary".
42	
43	The image search (`network.md`, `CatalogSearcher`, DEVDESK-306) reads the same
44	pair: it walks the catalog of the entry's host (`/v2/_catalog`, with the entry's
45	`auth_mode` through `credsFor`), keeps the names under `<repo_prefix>/` and
46	matches the typed text on the part after it. A catalog with no name under the
47	prefix is refused, not "no result". Entries that share an API URL and an
48	identity share one walk per search (DEVDESK-311, `network.md`); an entry with
49	other credentials, another port or another subdomain is walked on its own.
50	
51	Three things follow, each with a test:
52	
53	- **The prefix is applied once**, in `submitSearch`. It is then already part of
54	  `MultiRegistryTag.Repo`, so `multiImageName` and `registryAPIURL` know nothing
55	  about it — teaching both would be two places free to drift.
56	- **A group may not declare one**, and `LoadContext` refuses it: a group is
57	  reachable only through its own connector, and the same trick applied to a group
58	  answers 404. `RegistryForm` therefore does not offer the field on a group.
59	- **A URL no longer identifies an entry.** Several entries share one host now, so
60	  `entryFor` resolves by entry key, `resultFilter` holds a key, every
61	  `MultiRegistryTag` carries one, and `memberKey` takes the prefix as a third
62	  segment — a member's URL is its *group's*. `registryRef(url, prefix)` is the one
63	  place an entry becomes something a user reads, and it is the head of the pull
64	  reference exactly.
65	
66	`NexusDetector` synthesises nothing any more. A group written as a path prefix
67	serves its members the same way, so it emits `(host, memberName)` — consistent by
68	construction. Reached through a connector of its own it emits the group's URL and
69	**no** prefix, because which connector a member answers on is precisely what it
70	cannot read: an empty prefix against a bare host is wrong and visibly so, where
71	the synthesised path was wrong and plausible.
72	
73	**`auth_mode` is read before any credential lookup**, on both paths that talk to
74	a registry: `detectRegistryGroupCmd` and the browser's `credsFor`. `anonymous`
75	sends nothing, not even a configured username. This is what `auth_enabled` never
76	did (D12): `docker login` is keyed on host, so one login against a Nexus
77	instance used to authenticate every repository it serves.
78	
79	That same host-keying is why a **member cannot declare `credentials` of its
80	own** — it shares its group's single credential entry, so a password of its own
81	has nowhere to go — and why `inherit` on an entry with no group is refused.
82	Both are load-time errors.
83	
84	`internal/config/registries.go` normalizes the list at load and is the only
85	place that decides a slug. Two rules hold it together:
86	
87	- A slug **DevDesk derives** (from the alias, else the URL host) is made unique
88	  by stepping aside — `prod`, `prod-2`. A slug **the file declares** is never
89	  rewritten, because it is a link target; a duplicate, or a `parent` naming no
90	  configured group, makes `LoadContext` fail rather than load a config the
91	  application cannot honour.
92	- An entry from before `kind` existed that carries a `management_url`, **or**
93	  whose URL contains `/repository/`, migrates to `kind: group`,
94	  `provider: nexus` — those were the two things `NexusDetector.CanHandle` used
95	  to accept. A kind the file states is never second-guessed.
96	
97	`provider` is what picks the detector in `internal/registrymgr`: `DetectGroup`
98	matches `Detector.Provider()` against the declared value and falls back to
99	`GenericDetector`, which discovers nothing. A registry is probed because it was
100	declared as something, never because its URL looked like it — so registration
101	order decides nothing, and a plain registry costs no HTTP call. The provider
102	names are stated in both packages on purpose; `TestTheProviderVocabularyMatchesTheConfig`
103	keeps them in step.
104	
105	`RegistryForm` is what keeps the file loadable: it refuses a duplicate or
106	badly-formed slug instead of correcting it, and drops the group-only fields when
107	the kind is not a group.
108	
109	
110	## Where the login lives — the `Logged` column
111	
112	`docker.RegistryLoginState` reads the engine's auth file and answers three
113	ways: no credentials, credentials held by a helper (`credsStore` /
114	`credHelpers`), or a secret **inline** in the file — base64, which is not
115	encryption. The `Logged` cell is `IconOK`, `IconWarning`, or `IconError`
116	accordingly, and the footer names the file while an inline row is selected.
117	DevDesk never wrote that secret (`login` goes through the CLI) and cannot move
118	it; saying so is all it can do (§3.68).
119	
120	What `login` writes differs between engines, measured rather than assumed:
121	docker leaves an empty `auths` entry behind a helper, podman leaves none under
122	`credHelpers` and ignores `credsStore` entirely. Both run
123	`docker-credential-<name>` helpers — podman has no prefix of its own (D73).
124	
125	## Registry group cache
126	
127	`internal/cache/registry_groups.go` — `RegistryGroupCache`, keyed by **group
128	slug**, metadata at `~/.devdesk/cache/registry-groups.json`. It holds the members
129	one discovery found and when: discovered members are derived data with a server
130	as their source of truth, and `config.yaml` is what the user declares.
131	
132	- Discovery runs **only for `kind: group`**, and only when asked: `ctrl+r` on a
133	  group row in the Registries tab. `detectRegistryGroupCmd` writes through.
134	- An empty result **is** stored — "asked, and it is not a group" is an answer.
135	  A *failed* one is not: an unreachable manager must not erase what was last
136	  known, which is why `registrymgr` distinguishes the two (D23).
137	- **The Nexus detector does not follow a redirect to another origin
138	  (DEVDESK-412).** Its client refuses it (`oci.RefuseOffOriginRedirect`), so
139	  the account is never sent to a host it was not given for. That includes the
140	  redirect from `http` to `https` of the same host: the origin differs, so enter
141	  the registry URL in `https`. A refused redirect is a failed discovery (D23): no
142	  members, the cached ones stay, and the log says the redirect was refused. The
143	  anonymous retry of the members endpoint starts on any error except this
144	  refusal. Each Nexus reply is read up to 1 MiB (`maxNexusResponse`, not
145	  measured); a larger one is an error, not a silent cut. A format endpoint that
146	  is too large or fails (other than the origin refusal) is logged with the
147	  advice `account may lack nx-repository-admin privilege`; the origin refusal
148	  has its own log message, without that advice. Either way no members come
149	  back.
150	- **A Nexus reply that is not a repository document is a failed discovery
151	  (DEVDESK-509).** A non-200 status is a typed error shown as
152	  `management API returned N` (it was `HTTP N`); an empty body, invalid JSON or
153	  JSON with no `type` (`{}`, `null`) is an error too, not "not a group". Neither
154	  is cached (D23), so the cached members stay. A cancelled or timed-out request
155	  reports the context's error, never a status error.
156	- The `Members` column shows `count · TimeAgo(discovered_at)`, or `never`. It is
157	  not decoration: a cache with no visible age looks current whatever it holds.
158	- The **registry browser reads this cache**, never the network: it opens on the
159	  first frame and works offline. `→` on a group row in the Registries tab drills
160	  into its members, `←`/`esc` go back.
161	- **The image search (level 1) reads the same entries, keys and credentials**
162	  as the tag flow, and the selection applies to both form actions, Search and
163	  Open Tags (`submit(action)`, `network.md`): the checked entries (`selected(entry)`, D40), `credsFor`
164	  (anonymous stays anonymous, D12) and the entry's repository prefix (D39). It
165	  writes nothing: the remembered selection is unchanged (`network.md`).
166	  `→` on a level 1 row goes to that row's registry only, whatever the
167	  selection (DEVDESK-304, `network.md`). Each checked entry gets one verdict per
168	  search (DEVDESK-303), and `dhi.io` is refused without a request (`network.md`).
169	- `internal/cache/browser_selection.go` remembers what the browser had
170	  **un**checked, per context. Storing the exceptions is what makes a
171	  newly-discovered member arrive checked rather than silently excluded.
172	- **A picker entry is identified by `browserRegistryEntry.key`, never by its
173	  URL** (D40). Two registries may be declared on one host — the form enforces
174	  slug uniqueness, not URL uniqueness — so a URL ticks and unticks both, and the
175	  exclusion outlives the session. The key is the slug for a standalone registry
176	  and `memberKey(groupSlug, memberURL)` for a member; `Slug` alone will not do,
177	  since a member carries its *group's*. Read it through `selected(entry)` rather
178	  than indexing `selectedRegs` at a new site.
179

systemPrompt:
Tu es architecte logiciel. Tu conçois ; tu n'implémentes pas (tu n'écris que dans `docs/`).

## Méthode

1. Lis le code existant et les contraintes (`CLAUDE.md`, ADR, infra) avant de proposer.
   Si le brief contient une synthèse du wiki (« Références wiki », produite par
   `dev-team:wiki-scout`), appuie les options dessus et cite-la. Ne parcours pas le wiki
   toi-même : lis au plus une page, à partir d'un chemin donné dans la synthèse, pour
   approfondir un point précis. Sans synthèse, continue normalement.
2. Exprime les exigences non fonctionnelles (charge, sécurité, coût, exploitabilité).
3. Compare au moins deux options avec leurs compromis, puis recommande-en une.
4. Décris composants, interfaces, flux de données, modèle de données, migration.
5. Identifie risques et points irréversibles.

## Documentation à jour (Context7)

Si les outils `mcp__plugin_dev-team_context7__*` sont disponibles, vérifie avec eux les capacités et limites actuelles d'une bibliothèque ou d'un service avant de les recommander :
`resolve-library-id` puis `query-docs`, avec une question précise (une bibliothèque, un
sujet, la version du projet), jamais « toute la documentation ». Sinon, lis le code et les
manifestes du projet, ou demande : ne devine pas une signature d'API.

## Mode faisabilité rapide

Sur un brief produit ou des stories, sans conception détaillée : faisable ou non et à
quelles conditions, risques techniques majeurs, dépendances externes, effort par story
(S / M / L, avec l'hypothèse qui le justifie), stories à redécouper et comment.
Une page au plus ; pas d'ADR ; pas de wiki.

## Sortie (conception)

- Brouillon d'ADR si la décision le mérite (skill `team-core:adr` si disponible : critères,
  gabarit), à archiver par `archivist`.
- Plan d'implémentation : étapes numérotées, chacune livrable et testable seule, avec
  fichiers concernés, interfaces à créer (signatures), comportements à tester
  (entrée → résultat attendu, cas d'erreur), dépendances entre étapes et critère de fin.
  Le `tester` écrit les tests de l'étape avant le code à partir de ces éléments. Signale les étapes
  parallélisables. Un `coder` doit pouvoir réaliser une étape sans relire tout le plan.

## Ne rien supposer

Si une information qui change le résultat manque ou est ambiguë (volumétrie, exigence non fonctionnelle, contrainte d'hébergement, choix qui engage l'utilisateur ; ne chiffre jamais une charge inventée), ne la devine
pas : arrête-toi et rends tes questions en tête de ta sortie, sous **Questions
bloquantes**, chacune avec les options possibles et ta recommandation. L'orchestrateur
les posera à l'utilisateur. Pour un détail sans conséquence, choisis l'option la plus
prudente et signale-la dans ta sortie (`Hypothèse : …`).

tools.description:
Executes a bash command and returns its output.

- `cd` carries to the next call only in the main session, if the command succeeds and ends inside the working directories. Outside them the shell returns to the start folder; otherwise it stays where it was. Prefer absolute paths — `cd` in a compound command can trigger a permission prompt. Shell state (env vars, functions) does not persist; the shell is initialized from the user's profile.
- IMPORTANT: Avoid using this tool to run `cat`, `head`, `tail`, `sed`, `awk`, or `echo` commands, unless explicitly instructed or after you have verified that a dedicated tool cannot accomplish your task. Instead, use the appropriate dedicated tool as this will provide a much better experience for the user.
- Command output is displayed to you, not reliably to the user.
- `timeout` is in milliseconds: default 120000, max 600000 for a foreground command.
- `run_in_background` runs the command detached: it keeps running across turns and re-invokes you when it exits. With it, `timeout` is how long the command may run in the background (default 1800000, max 7200000); at that limit it is stopped and you are re-invoked. No `&` needed. Foreground `sleep` is blocked; use Monitor with an until-loop to wait on a condition.

1	package registrymgr
2	
3	import "context"
4	
5	// The repository managers a group may declare. These repeat the values in
6	// internal/config on purpose: config owns what a config file may say, this
7	// package owns what can actually be detected, and neither should have to import
8	// the other to say so. TestTheProviderVocabularyMatchesTheConfig pins them
9	// together.
10	const (
11		ProviderGeneric     = "generic"
12		ProviderNexus       = "nexus"
13		ProviderHarbor      = "harbor"
14		ProviderArtifactory = "artifactory"
15		ProviderGitLab      = "gitlab"
16	)
17	
18	// GroupMember represents a single member of a registry group.
19	//
20	// A member is an *address*, not a URL: `(URL, RepoPrefix)` is the pair browse and
21	// pull both derive from, which is what stops them meaning two different
22	// repositories (D39, §3.18). RepoPrefix is empty when the detector cannot know
23	// how the member is reached, and empty is the honest answer there — an empty
24	// prefix against a bare host is wrong and visibly so, where a synthesised path
25	// is wrong and plausible.
26	type GroupMember struct {
27		Alias      string
28		URL        string
29		RepoPrefix string
30	}
31	
32	// RegistryInfo carries the information needed for group detection.
33	// ManagementURL is optional: set it when the Docker registry URL differs from
34	// the URL the repository manager exposes for its API (group discovery, etc.).
35	type RegistryInfo struct {
36		// Provider is the declared repository manager, and it is what picks the
37		// detector. It is not sniffed from the URL: guessing made the detector list
38		// effectively single-vendor and probed registries that had never claimed to
39		// be one (§3.8, decision F).
40		Provider      string
41		URL           string
42		ManagementURL string
43		Username      string
44		Password      string
45	}
46	
47	// Detector enumerates the members of a group repository for one provider.
48	type Detector interface {
49		// Provider returns the declared provider this detector serves.
50		Provider() string
51		// DetectGroup returns the group members when the registry is a group repo.
52		// Returns nil, nil when the registry is not a group (not an error).
53		DetectGroup(ctx context.Context, info RegistryInfo) ([]GroupMember, error)
54	}
55	
56	var detectors []Detector
57	
58	// Register adds a Detector to the global registry.
59	// Implementations call this from their init() function.
60	func Register(d Detector) {
61		detectors = append(detectors, d)
62	}
63	
64	// DetectGroup dispatches to the detector serving info.Provider, falling back to
65	// the generic one — which discovers nothing — for a provider no detector
66	// implements. Registration order does not matter: the match is on a declared
67	// value, and the fallback is chosen only when nothing claims it.
68	func DetectGroup(ctx context.Context, info RegistryInfo) ([]GroupMember, error) {
69		var fallback Detector
70		for _, d := range detectors {
71			if d.Provider() == info.Provider && info.Provider != "" {
72				return d.DetectGroup(ctx, info)
73			}
74			if d.Provider() == ProviderGeneric {
75				fallback = d
76			}
77		}
78		if fallback == nil {
79			return nil, nil
80		}
81		return fallback.DetectGroup(ctx, info)
82	}

## Code editing instructions

### Rule 201 : Code must be clean, concise, and well-structured to stay maintainable

#### Extracting functions from Update()
- **Strict limit**: If a case in `Update(msg tea.Msg)` exceeds **5 lines**, extract it into a separate function
- **Naming**: `handle[MessageType]` (e.g. `handleContextSwitch()`, `handleKeyPress()`)
- **Pattern**: The function must return `(tea.Model, tea.Cmd)`

**Before (bad):**
```go
case ContextSwitchCompleteMsg:
    a.config = msg.Config
    a.currentContext = msg.ContextName
    a.reinitializeViews(msg.Config)
    return a, func() tea.Msg {
        return tea.WindowSizeMsg{Width: a.width, Height: a.height}
    }
```

**After (good):**
```go
case ContextSwitchCompleteMsg:
    return a.handleContextSwitch(msg)

// Further down in the file
func (a *App) handleContextSwitch(msg ContextSwitchCompleteMsg) (tea.Model, tea.Cmd) {
    a.config = msg.Config
    a.currentContext = msg.ContextName
    a.reinitializeViews(msg.Config)
    return a, func() tea.Msg {
        return tea.WindowSizeMsg{Width: a.width, Height: a.height}
    }
}
```

#### Code reuse
- **Zero duplication**: If a block of code appears 2+ times, create a function
- **Modules**: Group related functions together (e.g. all context switching in a single file)
- **Constants**: Extract magic values into named constants

#### Error handling
- **Bubble Tea pattern**: Errors = messages (e.g. `ContextSwitchErrorMsg`)
- **Always log** in DEBUG mode: `log.Printf("ERROR: %v", err)`
- **Never ignore**: If the error is non-critical, document why

#### Comments
- **Mandatory for**:
  - Exported (public) functions
  - Complex business logic
  - Workarounds or non-obvious decisions
- **Format**: `// functionName does X and returns Y`
- **Avoid**: Comments that repeat the code

#### Complexity
- **Maximum 3 levels of indentation** in a function
- **Functions > 50 lines**: refactor into smaller functions
- **Switch > 10 cases**: consider a table-driven pattern

1	package registrymgr
2	
3	import "context"
4	
5	// The repository managers a group may declare. These repeat the values in
6	// internal/config on purpose: config owns what a config file may say, this
7	// package owns what can actually be detected, and neither should have to import
8	// the other to say so. TestTheProviderVocabularyMatchesTheConfig pins them
9	// together.
10	const (
11		ProviderGeneric     = "generic"
12		ProviderNexus       = "nexus"
13		ProviderHarbor      = "harbor"
14		ProviderArtifactory = "artifactory"
15		ProviderGitLab      = "gitlab"
16	)
17	
18	// GroupMember represents a single member of a registry group.
19	//
20	// A member is an *address*, not a URL: `(URL, RepoPrefix)` is the pair browse and
21	// pull both derive from, which is what stops them meaning two different
22	// repositories (D39, §3.18). RepoPrefix is empty when the detector cannot know
23	// how the member is reached, and empty is the honest answer there — an empty
24	// prefix against a bare host is wrong and visibly so, where a synthesised path
25	// is wrong and plausible.
26	type GroupMember struct {
27		Alias      string
28		URL        string
29		RepoPrefix string
30	}
31	
32	// RegistryInfo carries the information needed for group detection.
33	// ManagementURL is optional: set it when the Docker registry URL differs from
34	// the URL the repository manager exposes for its API (group discovery, etc.).
35	type RegistryInfo struct {
36		// Provider is the declared repository manager, and it is what picks the
37		// detector. It is not sniffed from the URL: guessing made the detector list
38		// effectively single-vendor and probed registries that had never claimed to
39		// be one (§3.8, decision F).
40		Provider      string
41		URL           string
42		ManagementURL string
43		Username      string
44		Password      string
45	}
46	
47	// Detector enumerates the members of a group repository for one provider.
48	type Detector interface {
49		// Provider returns the declared provider this detector serves.
50		Provider() string
51		// DetectGroup returns the group members when the registry is a group repo.
52		// Returns nil, nil when the registry is not a group (not an error).
53		DetectGroup(ctx context.Context, info RegistryInfo) ([]GroupMember, error)
54	}
55	
56	var detectors []Detector
57	
58	// Register adds a Detector to the global registry.
59	// Implementations call this from their init() function.
60	func Register(d Detector) {
61		detectors = append(detectors, d)
62	}
63	
64	// DetectGroup dispatches to the detector serving info.Provider, falling back to
65	// the generic one — which discovers nothing — for a provider no detector
66	// implements. Registration order does not matter: the match is on a declared
67	// value, and the fallback is chosen only when nothing claims it.
68	func DetectGroup(ctx context.Context, info RegistryInfo) ([]GroupMember, error) {
69		var fallback Detector
70		for _, d := range detectors {
71			if d.Provider() == info.Provider && info.Provider != "" {
72				return d.DetectGroup(ctx, info)
73			}
74			if d.Provider() == ProviderGeneric {
75				fallback = d
76			}
77		}
78		if fallback == nil {
79			return nil, nil
80		}
81		return fallback.DetectGroup(ctx, info)
82	}

## Code quality rules and proactive checks

### Rule 301 : Systematic code quality check before commit

**MANDATORY**: Before creating a commit, ALWAYS perform the following checks:

#### 2. Tests

```bash
go test ./...
```

#### 3. Build

```bash
go build
```

**Required actions:**

- ✅ Test the application if functional changes were made

#### 4. Deprecated dependencies

**Detection:**
- Check golangci-lint SA1019 warnings

**Action:**

## Code editing instructions

### Rule 201 : Code must be clean, concise, and well-structured to stay maintainable

#### Extracting functions from Update()
- **Strict limit**: If a case in `Update(msg tea.Msg)` exceeds **5 lines**, extract it into a separate function
- **Naming**: `handle[MessageType]` (e.g. `handleContextSwitch()`, `handleKeyPress()`)
- **Pattern**: The function must return `(tea.Model, tea.Cmd)`

**Before (bad):**
```go
case ContextSwitchCompleteMsg:
    a.config = msg.Config
    a.currentContext = msg.ContextName
    a.reinitializeViews(msg.Config)
    return a, func() tea.Msg {
        return tea.WindowSizeMsg{Width: a.width, Height: a.height}
    }
```

**After (good):**
```go
case ContextSwitchCompleteMsg:
    return a.handleContextSwitch(msg)

// Further down in the file
func (a *App) handleContextSwitch(msg ContextSwitchCompleteMsg) (tea.Model, tea.Cmd) {
    a.config = msg.Config
    a.currentContext = msg.ContextName
    a.reinitializeViews(msg.Config)
    return a, func() tea.Msg {
        return tea.WindowSizeMsg{Width: a.width, Height: a.height}
    }
}
```

#### Code reuse
- **Zero duplication**: If a block of code appears 2+ times, create a function
- **Modules**: Group related functions together (e.g. all context switching in a single file)
- **Constants**: Extract magic values into named constants

#### Error handling
- **Bubble Tea pattern**: Errors = messages (e.g. `ContextSwitchErrorMsg`)
- **Always log** in DEBUG mode: `log.Printf("ERROR: %v", err)`
- **Never ignore**: If the error is non-critical, document why

#### Comments
- **Mandatory for**:
  - Exported (public) functions
  - Complex business logic
  - Workarounds or non-obvious decisions
- **Format**: `// functionName does X and returns Y`
- **Avoid**: Comments that repeat the code

#### Complexity
- **Maximum 3 levels of indentation** in a function
- **Functions > 50 lines**: refactor into smaller functions
- **Switch > 10 cases**: consider a table-driven pattern

</system-reminder>

  20 // RegistryGroupMember is one repository fronted by a group.

  22 // The pair (URL, RepoPrefix) is the member's address, and both halves are needed
  23 // because the prefix is what tells two members of one group apart once they no
  24 // longer each carry a synthesised URL of their own (§3.18). An entry written
  25 // before the field existed decodes to an empty prefix, which is what it meant.
  26 type RegistryGroupMember struct {
  27     Alias      string `json:"alias"`
  28     URL        string `json:"url"`
  29     RepoPrefix string `json:"repo_prefix,omitempty"`

  31 
  32 // RegistryGroupEntry is the result of one discovery. An entry with no members
  33 // is a real answer — "asked, and it is not a group" — and is what keeps a
  34 // non-group from being probed forever.
  35 type RegistryGroupEntry struct {
  36     Members      []RegistryGroupMember `json:"members"`
  37     DiscoveredAt time.Time             `json:"discovered_at"`
  38 }
  39 
  40 // RegistryGroupCache manages the discovered-members cache file.
  41 type RegistryGroupCache struct {
  42     mu      sync.RWMutex
  43     path    string
  44     entries map[string]RegistryGroupEntry // keyed by group slug
  45 }
  46 
  47 // NewRegistryGroupCache creates or loads the cache from
  48 // ~/.devdesk/cache/registry-groups.json
  49 func NewRegistryGroupCache() (*RegistryGroupCache, error) {
  50     homeDir, err := os.UserHomeDir()
  51     if err != nil {
  52         return nil, err
  53     }
  54 
  55     cacheDir := filepath.Join(homeDir, ".devdesk", "cache")
  56     if err := os.MkdirAll(cacheDir, 0755); err != nil {
  57         return nil, err
  58     }
  59 
  60     c := &RegistryGroupCache{
  61         path:    filepath.Join(cacheDir, "registry-groups.json"),
  62         entries: make(map[string]RegistryGroupEntry),
  63     }
  64 
  65     c.load()
  66     return c, nil
  67 }
  68 
  69 // load reads the cache file from disk
  70 func (c *RegistryGroupCache) load() {
  71     data, err := os.ReadFile(c.path)
  72     if err != nil {
  73         return
  74     }
  75     if err := json.Unmarshal(data, &c.entries); err != nil {

  82     data, err := json.MarshalIndent(c.entries, "", "  ")

  91     c.mu.RLock()

84	// its result) as well as a network call, and this server does neither.

113				}

A context error is never a `StatusError`: a failed body read returns `read Nexus response: <ctx error>` (wrapped with `%w`) when the context is done, so `errors.Is(err, context.Canceled | context.DeadlineExceeded)` holds whatever `net/http` returns. (Q3) an `http://` Bearer realm behind an `https` registry is refused, with or without credentials (this closes D142's residual risk of the clear-text realm); a realm that is neither `http` nor `https` is refused too. (Q4) the registry URL is redacted in `browser_bridge.go` and in the error prefixes of `registry.go` (`RedactURL`; closes D142's raw-URL residual risk). (Q5a) the digest of the layer is always checked, redirected or not: `sha256:` and 64 lowercase hex digits only, so a registry whose layers are `sha512` is refused. Incident of 2026-11-16 17:21: a test with an endless, uncapped reader exhausted the memory of the machine (OOM). Rule for tests that follows: never serve or read an endless body without a cap; bound it with a sentinel error (a reader that fails after N bytes, a handler that stops on the first write error), never rely on the timeout. 101:**D160 — DEVDESK-509 (NX-06): the Nexus REST client handles errors like the `internal/oci` registry client. Decided (plan `.claude/plans/DEVDESK-509-plan.md`, 2026-11-17): (1) The client reuses `internal/oci`: a third source, `oci.SourceManagementAPI`, in `oci.StatusError` (`management API returned <code>`), for a registry manager's own REST API. No copy, no new package, no import cycle (`internal/oci` depends on no other `devdesk` package). Rejected: a `registrymgr.StatusError` (a second type for one concept) and an extracted `internal/httpguard` (out of proportion here). (2) A non-200 answer is a `*oci.StatusError` with no status line, body or header echoed, so no secret reaches the error. A context error is never a `StatusError`: a failed body read returns `read Nexus response: <ctx error>` (wrapped with `%w`) when the context is done, so `errors.Is(err, context.Canceled | context.DeadlineExceeded)` holds whatever `net/http` returns. (3) The 1 MiB reply cap (`maxNexusResponse`) stays in `nexus.go`, not shared with the token cap (`maxTokenResponse`), which bounds another reply. (4) Behaviour change: a 200 reply that is empty, or valid JSON with no `type` (`{}`, `null`), is a failed discovery (`errEmptyReply`, `errNoRepositoryType`, wrapped with the endpoint), not cached as "not a group" (D23); the members last known are kept. Hypothesis, to confirm in review: Nexus always sends `type` on `GET /service/rest/v1/repositories/{name}`. Syntax errors were already rejected. Story: `docs/product/nexus-support/stories.md`, NX-07. Depends on NX-06
(DEVDESK-509, D160, merged). Effort: **M, confirmed** (6 steps, two of them
parallel; the UI step waits for the UX text).

| Where | What it does today | Defect |
|---|---|---|

## Non-functional requirements

- **No secret in any error, log or screen** (D160 (2)): the refusal carries the
  status code and the Nexus repository name only, never the URL, a header or a body.
- **D23 holds**: anything that is not a settled listing writes nothing over the
  members last known.
- **Rule 110**: the Cmd does network and disk I/O and returns a message; only
  `Update` (the handler) changes the model.
- **No new request**: the number of HTTP calls per discovery is unchanged (1, 2 or
  3 with the anonymous retry). No load figure is needed: one discovery per
  `ctrl+r` on one group row.
- **Rollback**: a revert must leave a usable cache (see "Downgrade" below).

## Decisions

### D1. Outcome of step 2: three cases, the refusal is a typed error

| Step-2 result | `DetectGroup` returns | Cached? |
|---|---|---|
| 200, `{"group":{"memberNames":[...]}}` (possibly `[]`) | `members, nil` (`[]GroupMember{}` for `[]`) | yes, settled (CA2) |
| authenticated (or the only) attempt answered **401 or 403** by the management API, and the anonymous retry did not succeed | `nil, *MembersRefusedError` (`errors.Is(err, ErrMembersRefused)`, `errors.As(err, **oci.StatusError)`) | **no listing written**; a refusal record is written beside it (D3) |
| context error (cancel, deadline), network error, other status (404, 5xx), off-origin redirect, unreadable 200 reply | `nil, wrapped error` (`errors.Is(err, context.DeadlineExceeded)`, `oci.ErrOffOriginRedirect`, `*oci.StatusError` with another code, `errNoGroupDocument`…) | nothing written (CA3, D23) |

**Shape chosen** (new file `internal/registrymgr/refusal.go`):

```go
// ErrMembersRefused marks a group whose repository manager said it is a group
// and then refused to list its members to the account that asked.
var ErrMembersRefused = errors.New("group members refused")

// MembersRefusedError is that refusal, with what a screen needs to explain it.
type MembersRefusedError struct {
    Group     string // repository name in the manager (path segment, no URL)
    Status    int    // 401 or 403
    Anonymous bool   // the refused request carried no credential
    Cause     error  // the *oci.StatusError (Source: SourceManagementAPI)
}

func (e *MembersRefusedError) Error() string        // "reading the members of group %q: management API returned 403"
func (e *MembersRefusedError) Unwrap() error        // e.Cause
func (e *MembersRefusedError) Is(target error) bool // target == ErrMembersRefused
```

| Option | For | Against |
|---|---|---|
| **A. typed error + sentinel via `Is` (chosen)** | CA1 asks for `errors.Is`/`errors.As`; the D23 rule in `detectRegistryGroupCmd` (`err == nil` ⇒ cache) already does "not cached as 0 members" for free; carries `Status`/`Anonymous` for the UX text; `Detector` interface unchanged | the caller must tell a refusal from other errors (one `errors.As`) |
| B. bare sentinel, `fmt.Errorf("%w: %w", ErrMembersRefused, statusErr)` | smallest | cannot say whether the refused request was anonymous (the caller cannot infer it once the anonymous retry ran) |
| C. result struct `Discovery{Members, Outcome}` replacing `([]GroupMember, error)` | outcome explicit, not an error | changes `Detector`, `GenericDetector`, `DetectGroup`, every caller and ~40 tests; CA1 wants the cause through `errors.Is/As` anyway |

**Which attempt decides.** The anonymous retry policy of D156 is kept as is (it
runs on any error except an off-origin refusal). The verdict is the **first
attempt's** unless the retry succeeds:

- retry succeeds → members (settled), as today (`TestNexusAnonymousRetryAfterARefusedAccountStays`);
- first attempt 401/403 → `MembersRefusedError{Anonymous: !hasAuth}`, whatever the
  retry got (a redirect, a 403, a timeout): the account *was* refused, and that is
  the actionable fact. The retry's error is logged, not returned;
- first attempt anything else → that error, wrapped with the endpoint
  (`fmt.Errorf("reading %s: %w", endpoint, err)`, same form as `fetchRepoMeta`).

Hypothèse : 401 and 403 are "refused"; 404 on the format endpoint is a failed
discovery, not a refusal (an older Nexus or another format may not serve that
endpoint; nothing is cached, so the most prudent reading). To revisit after the
bench measure H2 (NX-03).

Hypothèse : a 200 format reply is a group document only if it has a `group`
object **and** a `memberNames` key (`[]` included). `null`, `{}`, `{"group":{}}`,
invalid JSON or an empty body → `errNoGroupDocument` / the `encoding/json` error,
a failed discovery (same reasoning as D160 (4)). Decoded with
`Group *struct{ MemberNames []string }` and a nil check on both levels (`[]`
decodes to a non-nil empty slice, absent/`null` to nil).

Hypothèse : a 401/403 on the **generic** endpoint (step 1) stays a plain failed
discovery, not `ErrMembersRefused`: we do not know yet that the repository is a
group. Pinned by a test so it does not drift.

### D2. Refusal is not a listing: the cache keeps listings and refusals apart

The refusal is stored **beside** the listings, not inside an entry:

```go
// internal/cache/registry_groups.go
type RegistryGroupRefusal struct {
    At        time.Time `json:"at"`
    Status    int       `json:"status"`
    Anonymous bool      `json:"anonymous,omitempty"`
}
```

| Option | For | Against |
|---|---|---|
| **A. separate `refusals` map (chosen)** | "an entry is present" keeps meaning "a settled answer" for every reader (`membersCell`, `buildEntries`, MCP `discovery`, the existing fixtures with a zero `DiscoveredAt`); a refusal leaves the members last known untouched (D23); a later listing clears it | two maps to read |
| B. `Refused *RegistryGroupRefusal` inside `RegistryGroupEntry` | one map | a refused-only group becomes an entry with no members, which is the bug again for every reader that tests presence; each reader needs a new `Listed()` check |
| C. do not persist the refusal (footer only) | smallest | the Members column says `never` after a restart, the browser and MCP cannot tell; see Question 1 |

Rules: `Set(slug, entry)` stores a listing **and deletes** `refusals[slug]`;
`SetRefusal(slug, r)` stores a refusal and **does not touch** `groups[slug]`.

### D3. Cache file v2 and CA6

The repository's convention for a cache that changes shape is a versioned
envelope in the same file (`scan_file.go:8-24`, `image_scan.go:41-60`,
`remediation.go:28-32`). Same here, same path
`~/.devdesk/cache/registry-groups.json`:

```json
{ "version": 2,
  "groups":   { "<slug>": { "members": [...], "discovered_at": "..." } },
  "refusals": { "<slug>": { "at": "...", "status": 403, "anonymous": false } } }
```

`registryGroupCacheVersion = 2` (version 1 is the bare map, which has no
`version` key). One pure decoder used by both readers:

```go
// decodeRegistryGroupFile reads either shape. dropped counts the legacy entries
// set aside (CA6).
func decodeRegistryGroupFile(data []byte) (groups map[string]RegistryGroupEntry,
    refusals map[string]RegistryGroupRefusal, dropped int, err error)
```

- envelope decodes **and** `version >= 2` → use `groups`/`refusals` as they are
  (a `version > 2` from a newer build: read what decodes, unknown fields ignored);
- otherwise decode as the legacy bare map and **keep the entries with at least
  one member, drop the entries with none**. A non-empty legacy entry can only
  come from a successful read (a refusal never produced members), so it is
  trustworthy; an empty one may be a swallowed refusal and is indistinguishable
  from a real "0 members / not a group", so it becomes unknown (`never`) — CA6,
  no manual step. The cost: a real non-group or empty group shows `never` until
  the next `ctrl+r` on it;
- discriminate on `version >= 2`, not on `groups != nil`: a legacy map with a
  slug literally named `groups` or `version` must still be read as legacy.

`RegistryGroupCache.load` applies it in memory and logs `dropped` (count only);
the file is rewritten in v2 at the next `Set`/`SetRefusal`/`Delete` (no write on
read: unlike the scan cache there is no ownership to settle). `ReadRegistryGroups`
(MCP) applies the same decoder and never writes (`TestListingRegistriesDoesNotTouchTheGroupCache`).

Hypothèse : selective drop rather than dropping the whole legacy file (which
would lose real member lists and force a `ctrl+r` on every group).

**Downgrade** (revert or older binary): an old build unmarshals the envelope
into its bare map, gets a type error on `version`, logs it and sees keys
`groups`/`refusals` that match no slug: every group reads `never`. If it then
writes, the file is a bare map again; the new build reads it as legacy and drops
the junk keys (no member). Worst case is `never` + one `ctrl+r`, never a false
"0 members". Accepted.

### D4. Flow to the UI (Rule 110)

```
ctrl+r (Update) → refreshSelectedGroupCmd → detectRegistryGroupCmd   [Cmd]
   DetectGroup(ctx, info)
   at := time.Now()
   ├─ err == nil                → cacheGroupMembers(slug, members, at)      (disk: Set, clears refusal)
   ├─ errors.As(err, &refused)  → cacheGroupRefusal(slug, refusalRecord(refused, at)) (disk: SetRefusal)
   └─ other error               → nothing written
   return RegistryGroupDetectedMsg{RegistryURL, Slug, Members, Err, At: at}
Update → handleRegistryGroupDetected(msg)                              [model]
   ├─ success  → groupCache[slug] = entry; delete(groupRefusals, slug)
   ├─ refused  → groupRefusals[slug] = refusalRecord(refused, msg.At); footer.Warn(<UX text>)
   └─ other    → unchanged: footer.Error("Group refresh failed — check logs")
   updateRegistryTable()
Init → loadRegistryGroupCache (Cmd) → RegistryGroupCacheLoadedMsg{Entries, Refusals} → handler copies both
```

`refusalRecord(*registrymgr.MembersRefusedError, time.Time) cache.RegistryGroupRefusal`
is the one conversion, used by the Cmd (disk) and the handler (memory), so the two
cannot disagree (Rule 201, zero duplication). `msg.At` replaces the second
`time.Now()` in the handler (today `browser_bridge.go:175`), so disk and memory
hold the same instant.

  concurrent discoveries for different groups each open their own
  `RegistryGroupCache`, `load` then `Set`; the last writer wins and can erase the
  other's write. `SetRefusal` is one more writer. Out of scope; candidate
  follow-up (single cache instance owned by the model, or re-read under a file
  lock before write).

  404 or an empty list) on the format endpoint; Nexus always sends `memberNames`

  by the criteria.

survive the session?**

  one map, and without it the column says `never` after a restart, which is the

- (b) no, footer only (H1): drop `SetRefusal`, the `refusals` map, step 5 and H2–H4.

# DEVDESK-510 (NX-07) — a Nexus group whose members are refused is not taken for an empty group

Story: `docs/product/nexus-support/stories.md`, NX-07. Depends on NX-06
(DEVDESK-509, D160, merged). Effort: **M, confirmed** (6 steps, two of them
parallel; the UI step waits for the UX text).

## Starting point (read on `main`, `dce74805`)

| Where | What it does today | Defect |
|---|---|---|
| `internal/registrymgr/nexus.go:97-101` (`DetectGroup`, step 2) | `members = n.fetchGroupMembers(...)`; `return members, nil` | any step-2 failure becomes "0 members", a settled answer |
| `internal/registrymgr/nexus.go:154-188` (`fetchGroupMembers`) | returns `[]GroupMember` only; `return nil` on off-origin refusal (`:170-174`), on any status or network error (`:175-178`), on invalid JSON (`:184-186`) | 403, 5xx, timeout, unreadable reply, off-origin redirect: all read as "0 members" |
| `internal/ui/oci_resources/commands.go:513-516` (`detectRegistryGroupCmd`) | `if err == nil { cacheGroupMembers(...) }` | correct (D23), but receives `err == nil` for all the above, so it **overwrites the members last known with an empty list** (D160 follow-up) |
| `internal/cache/registry_groups.go:35-38, 70-87` | bare JSON map `slug → {members, discovered_at}`, no version | an empty entry written by the bug is indistinguishable from a real "0 members / not a group" (CA6) |
| `internal/cache/readonly.go:155-174` (`ReadRegistryGroups`) | MCP's read-only reader, same bare map | same |
| `internal/ui/oci_resources/browser_bridge.go:161-180` (`handleRegistryGroupDetected`) | `Err != nil` → `footer.Error("Group refresh failed — check logs")`; success → `m.groupCache[slug] = …` | no refusal case |
| `internal/ui/oci_resources/table.go:414-427` (`membersCell`) | `never` / `N · age` / `refreshing` | no refusal state |
| `internal/ui/oci_resources/registries.go:33-35` (`enterSelectedGroup`) | "No members discovered yet — press ctrl+r to look" | after a refusal, ctrl+r cannot help: wrong advice |
| `internal/mcp/registry_tools.go:38-48, 85-137` (`registries_list`) | `discovery` present ⇔ an entry is cached | would report a refused group as "probed, 0 members" if the refusal were stored as an entry |

Tests that pin the current (wrong) behaviour and will flip:
`nexus_errors_test.go:290-318` (`TestNexusUnreadableFormatReplyGivesNoMembers`, its
comment already says "NX-07"), `nexus_hardening_test.go:283-316`
(`TestNexusFormatEndpointRedirectOffOriginIsRefused` accepts `err == nil`),
`nexus_hardening_test.go:405-437` (`TestNexusAnonymousRetryDoesNotFollowAnOffOriginRedirect`
wants `err == nil`), `nexus_log_test.go:41-61`
(`TestNexusLogKeepsTheAdminAdviceOnARefusedAccount` wants `err == nil`).

## Non-functional requirements

- **No secret in any error, log or screen** (D160 (2)): the refusal carries the
  status code and the Nexus repository name only, never the URL, a header or a body.
- **D23 holds**: anything that is not a settled listing writes nothing over the
  members last known.
- **Rule 110**: the Cmd does network and disk I/O and returns a message; only
  `Update` (the handler) changes the model.
- **No new request**: the number of HTTP calls per discovery is unchanged (1, 2 or
  3 with the anonymous retry). No load figure is needed: one discovery per
  `ctrl+r` on one group row.
- **Rollback**: a revert must leave a usable cache (see "Downgrade" below).

## Decisions

### D1. Outcome of step 2: three cases, the refusal is a typed error

| Step-2 result | `DetectGroup` returns | Cached? |
|---|---|---|
| 200, `{"group":{"memberNames":[...]}}` (possibly `[]`) | `members, nil` (`[]GroupMember{}` for `[]`) | yes, settled (CA2) |
| authenticated (or the only) attempt answered **401 or 403** by the management API, and the anonymous retry did not succeed | `nil, *MembersRefusedError` (`errors.Is(err, ErrMembersRefused)`, `errors.As(err, **oci.StatusError)`) | **no listing written**; a refusal record is written beside it (D3) |
| context error (cancel, deadline), network error, other status (404, 5xx), off-origin redirect, unreadable 200 reply | `nil, wrapped error` (`errors.Is(err, context.DeadlineExceeded)`, `oci.ErrOffOriginRedirect`, `*oci.StatusError` with another code, `errNoGroupDocument`…) | nothing written (CA3, D23) |

**Shape chosen** (new file `internal/registrymgr/refusal.go`):

```go
// ErrMembersRefused marks a group whose repository manager said it is a group
// and then refused to list its members to the account that asked.
var ErrMembersRefused = errors.New("group members refused")

// MembersRefusedError is that refusal, with what a screen needs to explain it.
type MembersRefusedError struct {
    Group     string // repository name in the manager (path segment, no URL)
    Status    int    // 401 or 403
    Anonymous bool   // the refused request carried no credential
    Cause     error  // the *oci.StatusError (Source: SourceManagementAPI)
}

func (e *MembersRefusedError) Error() string        // "reading the members of group %q: management API returned 403"
func (e *MembersRefusedError) Unwrap() error        // e.Cause
func (e *MembersRefusedError) Is(target error) bool // target == ErrMembersRefused
```

| Option | For | Against |
|---|---|---|
| **A. typed error + sentinel via `Is` (chosen)** | CA1 asks for `errors.Is`/`errors.As`; the D23 rule in `detectRegistryGroupCmd` (`err == nil` ⇒ cache) already does "not cached as 0 members" for free; carries `Status`/`Anonymous` for the UX text; `Detector` interface unchanged | the caller must tell a refusal from other errors (one `errors.As`) |
| B. bare sentinel, `fmt.Errorf("%w: %w", ErrMembersRefused, statusErr)` | smallest | cannot say whether the refused request was anonymous (the caller cannot infer it once the anonymous retry ran) |
| C. result struct `Discovery{Members, Outcome}` replacing `([]GroupMember, error)` | outcome explicit, not an error | changes `Detector`, `GenericDetector`, `DetectGroup`, every caller and ~40 tests; CA1 wants the cause through `errors.Is/As` anyway |

**Which attempt decides.** The anonymous retry policy of D156 is kept as is (it
runs on any error except an off-origin refusal). The verdict is the **first
attempt's** unless the retry succeeds:

- retry succeeds → members (settled), as today (`TestNexusAnonymousRetryAfterARefusedAccountStays`);
- first attempt 401/403 → `MembersRefusedError{Anonymous: !hasAuth}`, whatever the
  retry got (a redirect, a 403, a timeout): the account *was* refused, and that is
  the actionable fact. The retry's error is logged, not returned;
- first attempt anything else → that error, wrapped with the endpoint
  (`fmt.Errorf("reading %s: %w", endpoint, err)`, same form as `fetchRepoMeta`).

Hypothèse : 401 and 403 are "refused"; 404 on the format endpoint is a failed
discovery, not a refusal (an older Nexus or another format may not serve that
endpoint; nothing is cached, so the most prudent reading). To revisit after the
bench measure H2 (NX-03).

Hypothèse : a 200 format reply is a group document only if it has a `group`
object **and** a `memberNames` key (`[]` included). `null`, `{}`, `{"group":{}}`,
invalid JSON or an empty body → `errNoGroupDocument` / the `encoding/json` error,
a failed discovery (same reasoning as D160 (4)). Decoded with
`Group *struct{ MemberNames []string }` and a nil check on both levels (`[]`
decodes to a non-nil empty slice, absent/`null` to nil).

Hypothèse : a 401/403 on the **generic** endpoint (step 1) stays a plain failed
discovery, not `ErrMembersRefused`: we do not know yet that the repository is a
group. Pinned by a test so it does not drift.

### D2. Refusal is not a listing: the cache keeps listings and refusals apart

The refusal is stored **beside** the listings, not inside an entry:

```go
// internal/cache/registry_groups.go
type RegistryGroupRefusal struct {
    At        time.Time `json:"at"`
    Status    int       `json:"status"`
    Anonymous bool      `json:"anonymous,omitempty"`
}
```

| Option | For | Against |
|---|---|---|
| **A. separate `refusals` map (chosen)** | "an entry is present" keeps meaning "a settled answer" for every reader (`membersCell`, `buildEntries`, MCP `discovery`, the existing fixtures with a zero `DiscoveredAt`); a refusal leaves the members last known untouched (D23); a later listing clears it | two maps to read |
| B. `Refused *RegistryGroupRefusal` inside `RegistryGroupEntry` | one map | a refused-only group becomes an entry with no members, which is the bug again for every reader that tests presence; each reader needs a new `Listed()` check |
| C. do not persist the refusal (footer only) | smallest | the Members column says `never` after a restart, the browser and MCP cannot tell; see Question 1 |

Rules: `Set(slug, entry)` stores a listing **and deletes** `refusals[slug]`;
`SetRefusal(slug, r)` stores a refusal and **does not touch** `groups[slug]`.

### D3. Cache file v2 and CA6

The repository's convention for a cache that changes shape is a versioned
envelope in the same file (`scan_file.go:8-24`, `image_scan.go:41-60`,
`remediation.go:28-32`). Same here, same path
`~/.devdesk/cache/registry-groups.json`:

```json
{ "version": 2,
  "groups":   { "<slug>": { "members": [...], "discovered_at": "..." } },
  "refusals": { "<slug>": { "at": "...", "status": 403, "anonymous": false } } }
```

`registryGroupCacheVersion = 2` (version 1 is the bare map, which has no
`version` key). One pure decoder used by both readers:

```go
// decodeRegistryGroupFile reads either shape. dropped counts the legacy entries
// set aside (CA6).
func decodeRegistryGroupFile(data []byte) (groups map[string]RegistryGroupEntry,
    refusals map[string]RegistryGroupRefusal, dropped int, err error)
```

- envelope decodes **and** `version >= 2` → use `groups`/`refusals` as they are
  (a `version > 2` from a newer build: read what decodes, unknown fields ignored);
- otherwise decode as the legacy bare map and **keep the entries with at least
  one member, drop the entries with none**. A non-empty legacy entry can only
  come from a successful read (a refusal never produced members), so it is
  trustworthy; an empty one may be a swallowed refusal and is indistinguishable
  from a real "0 members / not a group", so it becomes unknown (`never`) — CA6,
  no manual step. The cost: a real non-group or empty group shows `never` until
  the next `ctrl+r` on it;
- discriminate on `version >= 2`, not on `groups != nil`: a legacy map with a
  slug literally named `groups` or `version` must still be read as legacy.

`RegistryGroupCache.load` applies it in memory and logs `dropped` (count only);
the file is rewritten in v2 at the next `Set`/`SetRefusal`/`Delete` (no write on
read: unlike the scan cache there is no ownership to settle). `ReadRegistryGroups`
(MCP) applies the same decoder and never writes (`TestListingRegistriesDoesNotTouchTheGroupCache`).

Hypothèse : selective drop rather than dropping the whole legacy file (which
would lose real member lists and force a `ctrl+r` on every group).

**Downgrade** (revert or older binary): an old build unmarshals the envelope
into its bare map, gets a type error on `version`, logs it and sees keys
`groups`/`refusals` that match no slug: every group reads `never`. If it then
writes, the file is a bare map again; the new build reads it as legacy and drops
the junk keys (no member). Worst case is `never` + one `ctrl+r`, never a false
"0 members". Accepted.

### D4. Flow to the UI (Rule 110)

```
ctrl+r (Update) → refreshSelectedGroupCmd → detectRegistryGroupCmd   [Cmd]
   DetectGroup(ctx, info)
   at := time.Now()
   ├─ err == nil                → cacheGroupMembers(slug, members, at)      (disk: Set, clears refusal)
   ├─ errors.As(err, &refused)  → cacheGroupRefusal(slug, refusalRecord(refused, at)) (disk: SetRefusal)
   └─ other error               → nothing written
   return RegistryGroupDetectedMsg{RegistryURL, Slug, Members, Err, At: at}
Update → handleRegistryGroupDetected(msg)                              [model]
   ├─ success  → groupCache[slug] = entry; delete(groupRefusals, slug)
   ├─ refused  → groupRefusals[slug] = refusalRecord(refused, msg.At); footer.Warn(<UX text>)
   └─ other    → unchanged: footer.Error("Group refresh failed — check logs")
   updateRegistryTable()
Init → loadRegistryGroupCache (Cmd) → RegistryGroupCacheLoadedMsg{Entries, Refusals} → handler copies both
```

`refusalRecord(*registrymgr.MembersRefusedError, time.Time) cache.RegistryGroupRefusal`
is the one conversion, used by the Cmd (disk) and the handler (memory), so the two
cannot disagree (Rule 201, zero duplication). `msg.At` replaces the second
`time.Now()` in the handler (today `browser_bridge.go:175`), so disk and memory
hold the same instant.

`internal/ui/oci_resources/members_refused.go`, as pure functions of one value:

an empty group. (1) `registrymgr.MembersRefusedError` (`Is` `ErrMembersRefused`,
`Unwrap` → `*oci.StatusError`) for a 401/403 on `/v1/repositories/{format}/group/{name}`;
the first attempt decides unless the anonymous retry succeeds. Any other step-2
failure (network, deadline, 404, 5xx, off-origin redirect, unreadable reply) is
propagated and not cached (D23). Rejected: a bare sentinel (cannot say anonymous),
a result struct (interface churn). (2) The group cache file moves to an envelope
`version: 2` with `groups` and `refusals`; a refusal never overwrites a listing; a
listing clears the refusal. Legacy bare-map entries with no member are dropped
on read (CA6), entries with members kept. (3) Wording of the refusal lives in
`members_refused.go` (UX). No ADR: local, derived data, reversible (a revert reads
the v2 file as empty groups, `never`)."

- **Pre-existing lost-update race** (not introduced, slightly widened): two
  concurrent discoveries for different groups each open their own
  `RegistryGroupCache`, `load` then `Set`; the last writer wins and can erase the
  other's write. `SetRefusal` is one more writer. Out of scope; candidate
  follow-up (single cache instance owned by the model, or re-read under a file
  lock before write).
- **Hypotheses to measure on the bench (NX-03, H2)**: a pull account gets 403 (not
  404 or an empty list) on the format endpoint; Nexus always sends `memberNames`
  for a group.
- **Security notes for the reviewer, out of scope**: `format` comes from the
  server and is put unescaped into the step-2 path (`nexus.go:158`), same origin
  only; `nexus.go:140` logs `type`/`format` with `%s` (D160 follow-up, `%q`).
  Either can be folded into step 1 if the reviewer wants it; neither is required
  by the criteria.

## Questions

**Q1 (needed before step 4, not before steps 1-3 and 5): should the refusal
survive the session?**
- (a) yes, persisted beside the listing (D2 option A): the Members column, the
  status line, MCP and optionally the browser header can say it after a restart.
  **Recommended**: CA6 already forces a cache format change, so the extra cost is
  one map, and without it the column says `never` after a restart, which is the
  "absence read as emptiness" family of defects this story fixes.
- (b) no, footer only (H1): drop `SetRefusal`, the `refusals` map, step 5 and H2–H4.
  Smaller, but CA4's "Registries tab / header" is then only a 3-second footer.
The UX proposal in progress decides much of this: if it places the text anywhere
but the footer, (a) is required.

# DEVDESK-510 (NX-07) — a Nexus group whose members are refused is not taken for an empty group

Story: `docs/product/nexus-support/stories.md`, NX-07. Depends on NX-06
(DEVDESK-509, D160, merged). Effort: **M, confirmed** (6 steps, two of them
parallel; the UI step waits for the UX text).

## Starting point (read on `main`, `dce74805`)

| Where | What it does today | Defect |
|---|---|---|
| `internal/registrymgr/nexus.go:97-101` (`DetectGroup`, step 2) | `members = n.fetchGroupMembers(...)`; `return members, nil` | any step-2 failure becomes "0 members", a settled answer |
| `internal/registrymgr/nexus.go:154-188` (`fetchGroupMembers`) | returns `[]GroupMember` only; `return nil` on off-origin refusal (`:170-174`), on any status or network error (`:175-178`), on invalid JSON (`:184-186`) | 403, 5xx, timeout, unreadable reply, off-origin redirect: all read as "0 members" |
| `internal/ui/oci_resources/commands.go:513-516` (`detectRegistryGroupCmd`) | `if err == nil { cacheGroupMembers(...) }` | correct (D23), but receives `err == nil` for all the above, so it **overwrites the members last known with an empty list** (D160 follow-up) |
| `internal/cache/registry_groups.go:35-38, 70-87` | bare JSON map `slug → {members, discovered_at}`, no version | an empty entry written by the bug is indistinguishable from a real "0 members / not a group" (CA6) |
| `internal/cache/readonly.go:155-174` (`ReadRegistryGroups`) | MCP's read-only reader, same bare map | same |
| `internal/ui/oci_resources/browser_bridge.go:161-180` (`handleRegistryGroupDetected`) | `Err != nil` → `footer.Error("Group refresh failed — check logs")`; success → `m.groupCache[slug] = …` | no refusal case |
| `internal/ui/oci_resources/table.go:414-427` (`membersCell`) | `never` / `N · age` / `refreshing` | no refusal state |
| `internal/ui/oci_resources/registries.go:33-35` (`enterSelectedGroup`) | "No members discovered yet — press ctrl+r to look" | after a refusal, ctrl+r cannot help: wrong advice |
| `internal/mcp/registry_tools.go:38-48, 85-137` (`registries_list`) | `discovery` present ⇔ an entry is cached | would report a refused group as "probed, 0 members" if the refusal were stored as an entry |

Tests that pin the current (wrong) behaviour and will flip:
`nexus_errors_test.go:290-318` (`TestNexusUnreadableFormatReplyGivesNoMembers`, its
comment already says "NX-07"), `nexus_hardening_test.go:283-316`
(`TestNexusFormatEndpointRedirectOffOriginIsRefused` accepts `err == nil`),
`nexus_hardening_test.go:405-437` (`TestNexusAnonymousRetryDoesNotFollowAnOffOriginRedirect`
wants `err == nil`), `nexus_log_test.go:41-61`
(`TestNexusLogKeepsTheAdminAdviceOnARefusedAccount` wants `err == nil`).

## Non-functional requirements

- **No secret in any error, log or screen** (D160 (2)): the refusal carries the
  status code and the Nexus repository name only, never the URL, a header or a body.
- **D23 holds**: anything that is not a settled listing writes nothing over the
  members last known.
- **Rule 110**: the Cmd does network and disk I/O and returns a message; only
  `Update` (the handler) changes the model.
- **No new request**: the number of HTTP calls per discovery is unchanged (1, 2 or
  3 with the anonymous retry). No load figure is needed: one discovery per
  `ctrl+r` on one group row.
- **Rollback**: a revert must leave a usable cache (see "Downgrade" below).

## Decisions

### D1. Outcome of step 2: three cases, the refusal is a typed error

| Step-2 result | `DetectGroup` returns | Cached? |
|---|---|---|
| 200, `{"group":{"memberNames":[...]}}` (possibly `[]`) | `members, nil` (`[]GroupMember{}` for `[]`) | yes, settled (CA2) |
| authenticated (or the only) attempt answered **401 or 403** by the management API, and the anonymous retry did not succeed | `nil, *MembersRefusedError` (`errors.Is(err, ErrMembersRefused)`, `errors.As(err, **oci.StatusError)`) | **no listing written**; a refusal record is written beside it (D3) |
| context error (cancel, deadline), network error, other status (404, 5xx), off-origin redirect, unreadable 200 reply | `nil, wrapped error` (`errors.Is(err, context.DeadlineExceeded)`, `oci.ErrOffOriginRedirect`, `*oci.StatusError` with another code, `errNoGroupDocument`…) | nothing written (CA3, D23) |

**Shape chosen** (new file `internal/registrymgr/refusal.go`):

```go
// ErrMembersRefused marks a group whose repository manager said it is a group
// and then refused to list its members to the account that asked.
var ErrMembersRefused = errors.New("group members refused")

// MembersRefusedError is that refusal, with what a screen needs to explain it.
type MembersRefusedError struct {
    Group     string // repository name in the manager (path segment, no URL)
    Status    int    // 401 or 403
    Anonymous bool   // the refused request carried no credential
    Cause     error  // the *oci.StatusError (Source: SourceManagementAPI)
}

func (e *MembersRefusedError) Error() string        // "reading the members of group %q: management API returned 403"
func (e *MembersRefusedError) Unwrap() error        // e.Cause
func (e *MembersRefusedError) Is(target error) bool // target == ErrMembersRefused
```

| Option | For | Against |
|---|---|---|
| **A. typed error + sentinel via `Is` (chosen)** | CA1 asks for `errors.Is`/`errors.As`; the D23 rule in `detectRegistryGroupCmd` (`err == nil` ⇒ cache) already does "not cached as 0 members" for free; carries `Status`/`Anonymous` for the UX text; `Detector` interface unchanged | the caller must tell a refusal from other errors (one `errors.As`) |
| B. bare sentinel, `fmt.Errorf("%w: %w", ErrMembersRefused, statusErr)` | smallest | cannot say whether the refused request was anonymous (the caller cannot infer it once the anonymous retry ran) |
| C. result struct `Discovery{Members, Outcome}` replacing `([]GroupMember, error)` | outcome explicit, not an error | changes `Detector`, `GenericDetector`, `DetectGroup`, every caller and ~40 tests; CA1 wants the cause through `errors.Is/As` anyway |

**Which attempt decides.** The anonymous retry policy of D156 is kept as is (it
runs on any error except an off-origin refusal). The verdict is the **first
attempt's** unless the retry succeeds:

- retry succeeds → members (settled), as today (`TestNexusAnonymousRetryAfterARefusedAccountStays`);
- first attempt 401/403 → `MembersRefusedError{Anonymous: !hasAuth}`, whatever the
  retry got (a redirect, a 403, a timeout): the account *was* refused, and that is
  the actionable fact. The retry's error is logged, not returned;
- first attempt anything else → that error, wrapped with the endpoint
  (`fmt.Errorf("reading %s: %w", endpoint, err)`, same form as `fetchRepoMeta`).

Hypothèse : 401 and 403 are "refused"; 404 on the format endpoint is a failed
discovery, not a refusal (an older Nexus or another format may not serve that
endpoint; nothing is cached, so the most prudent reading). To revisit after the
bench measure H2 (NX-03).

Hypothèse : a 200 format reply is a group document only if it has a `group`
object **and** a `memberNames` key (`[]` included). `null`, `{}`, `{"group":{}}`,
invalid JSON or an empty body → `errNoGroupDocument` / the `encoding/json` error,
a failed discovery (same reasoning as D160 (4)). Decoded with
`Group *struct{ MemberNames []string }` and a nil check on both levels (`[]`
decodes to a non-nil empty slice, absent/`null` to nil).

Hypothèse : a 401/403 on the **generic** endpoint (step 1) stays a plain failed
discovery, not `ErrMembersRefused`: we do not know yet that the repository is a
group. Pinned by a test so it does not drift.

### D2. Refusal is not a listing: the cache keeps listings and refusals apart

The refusal is stored **beside** the listings, not inside an entry:

```go
// internal/cache/registry_groups.go
type RegistryGroupRefusal struct {
    At        time.Time `json:"at"`
    Status    int       `json:"status"`
    Anonymous bool      `json:"anonymous,omitempty"`
}
```

| Option | For | Against |
|---|---|---|
| **A. separate `refusals` map (chosen)** | "an entry is present" keeps meaning "a settled answer" for every reader (`membersCell`, `buildEntries`, MCP `discovery`, the existing fixtures with a zero `DiscoveredAt`); a refusal leaves the members last known untouched (D23); a later listing clears it | two maps to read |
| B. `Refused *RegistryGroupRefusal` inside `RegistryGroupEntry` | one map | a refused-only group becomes an entry with no members, which is the bug again for every reader that tests presence; each reader needs a new `Listed()` check |
| C. do not persist the refusal (footer only) | smallest | the Members column says `never` after a restart, the browser and MCP cannot tell; see Question 1 |

Rules: `Set(slug, entry)` stores a listing **and deletes** `refusals[slug]`;
`SetRefusal(slug, r)` stores a refusal and **does not touch** `groups[slug]`.

### D3. Cache file v2 and CA6

The repository's convention for a cache that changes shape is a versioned
envelope in the same file (`scan_file.go:8-24`, `image_scan.go:41-60`,
`remediation.go:28-32`). Same here, same path
`~/.devdesk/cache/registry-groups.json`:

```json
{ "version": 2,
  "groups":   { "<slug>": { "members": [...], "discovered_at": "..." } },
  "refusals": { "<slug>": { "at": "...", "status": 403, "anonymous": false } } }
```

`registryGroupCacheVersion = 2` (version 1 is the bare map, which has no
`version` key). One pure decoder used by both readers:

```go
// decodeRegistryGroupFile reads either shape. dropped counts the legacy entries
// set aside (CA6).
func decodeRegistryGroupFile(data []byte) (groups map[string]RegistryGroupEntry,
    refusals map[string]RegistryGroupRefusal, dropped int, err error)
```

- envelope decodes **and** `version >= 2` → use `groups`/`refusals` as they are
  (a `version > 2` from a newer build: read what decodes, unknown fields ignored);
- otherwise decode as the legacy bare map and **keep the entries with at least
  one member, drop the entries with none**. A non-empty legacy entry can only
  come from a successful read (a refusal never produced members), so it is
  trustworthy; an empty one may be a swallowed refusal and is indistinguishable
  from a real "0 members / not a group", so it becomes unknown (`never`) — CA6,
  no manual step. The cost: a real non-group or empty group shows `never` until
  the next `ctrl+r` on it;
- discriminate on `version >= 2`, not on `groups != nil`: a legacy map with a
  slug literally named `groups` or `version` must still be read as legacy.

`RegistryGroupCache.load` applies it in memory and logs `dropped` (count only);
the file is rewritten in v2 at the next `Set`/`SetRefusal`/`Delete` (no write on
read: unlike the scan cache there is no ownership to settle). `ReadRegistryGroups`
(MCP) applies the same decoder and never writes (`TestListingRegistriesDoesNotTouchTheGroupCache`).

Hypothèse : selective drop rather than dropping the whole legacy file (which
would lose real member lists and force a `ctrl+r` on every group).

**Downgrade** (revert or older binary): an old build unmarshals the envelope
into its bare map, gets a type error on `version`, logs it and sees keys
`groups`/`refusals` that match no slug: every group reads `never`. If it then
writes, the file is a bare map again; the new build reads it as legacy and drops
the junk keys (no member). Worst case is `never` + one `ctrl+r`, never a false
"0 members". Accepted.

### D4. Flow to the UI (Rule 110)

```
ctrl+r (Update) → refreshSelectedGroupCmd → detectRegistryGroupCmd   [Cmd]
   DetectGroup(ctx, info)
   at := time.Now()
   ├─ err == nil                → cacheGroupMembers(slug, members, at)      (disk: Set, clears refusal)
   ├─ errors.As(err, &refused)  → cacheGroupRefusal(slug, refusalRecord(refused, at)) (disk: SetRefusal)
   └─ other error               → nothing written
   return RegistryGroupDetectedMsg{RegistryURL, Slug, Members, Err, At: at}
Update → handleRegistryGroupDetected(msg)                              [model]
   ├─ success  → groupCache[slug] = entry; delete(groupRefusals, slug)
   ├─ refused  → groupRefusals[slug] = refusalRecord(refused, msg.At); footer.Warn(<UX text>)
   └─ other    → unchanged: footer.Error("Group refresh failed — check logs")
   updateRegistryTable()
Init → loadRegistryGroupCache (Cmd) → RegistryGroupCacheLoadedMsg{Entries, Refusals} → handler copies both
```

`refusalRecord(*registrymgr.MembersRefusedError, time.Time) cache.RegistryGroupRefusal`
is the one conversion, used by the Cmd (disk) and the handler (memory), so the two
cannot disagree (Rule 201, zero duplication). `msg.At` replaces the second
`time.Now()` in the handler (today `browser_bridge.go:175`), so disk and memory
hold the same instant.

### D5. UI hook points (text supplied by UX, not frozen here)

All refusal wording lives in **one new file**,
`internal/ui/oci_resources/members_refused.go`, as pure functions of one value:

```go
// groupRefusalView is everything the refusal wording may use.
type groupRefusalView struct {
    Refusal  cache.RegistryGroupRefusal // Status, Anonymous, At
    Known    int  // members last listed and still cached (0 if never listed)
    Declared int  // config entries whose parent is this group (CA5)
}

func refusedFooterText(v groupRefusalView) string   // H1: footer after a refused ctrl+r (level Warn, Rule 128)
func refusedMembersCell(v groupRefusalView) string  // H2: Members column, plain text (Rule 122)
func refusedStatusLine(v groupRefusalView) string   // H3: status line while the group row is selected (like inlineSecretLine)
func refusedDrillInText(v groupRefusalView) string  // H4: → on a refused group with no member listed
```

| Hook | Site | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| H1 footer | `browser_bridge.go:161-180` | one-shot message after the refresh |
| H2 Members cell | `table.go:414-427` `membersCell`; colour via the column's `Style` (`table.go:385-391`) reading a new `registryRow.membersRefused bool` (`table.go:357-368`) | plain text in `Cell` (Rule 122) |
| H3 status line | `view.go:115-141`, beside `inlineSecretLine`; first non-empty wins | a state, held while the row is selected |
| H4 drill-in | `registries.go:33-35` | replaces "press ctrl+r", which cannot help after a refusal |
| H5 Registries header (optional) | `view.go:299-302` | e.g. a count of refused groups; only if UX asks |
| H6 browser level-1 header (optional) | `browser_summary.go:155-200`, needs refusals passed to `newRegistryBrowser` (`registry_browser.go:291`, called from `browser_bridge.go:25`) | only if UX asks; not needed by the criteria |

Until UX answers, the coder uses placeholder English text that satisfies the
invariants the tests check (below); swapping the text is then a one-file change
with no test change beyond the golden strings, if UX wants any.

Invariants tested on every hook text (CA4): English (ASCII), mentions
`repo_prefix`, says the members could not be read (refusal, not "0" or "empty"),
contains neither `err.Error()` nor `management API returned`, nor the registry
URL; `Anonymous: true` is worded differently from an account refusal (UX picks
the words; the test only checks the two texts differ).

## Implementation plan

Steps 1 and 2 are independent and can run in parallel; step 5 needs only step 2.
Step 3 needs 1 and 2; step 4 needs 3 and the UX text (placeholders allowed).
Step 6 closes.

### Step 1 — `registrymgr`: step 2 returns a refusal or an error, never a silent "0" (CA1, CA2, CA3)

Draft D161: "DEVDESK-510 (NX-07): a refused members endpoint is a typed error, not
an empty group. (1) `registrymgr.MembersRefusedError` (`Is` `ErrMembersRefused`,
`Unwrap` → `*oci.StatusError`) for a 401/403 on `/v1/repositories/{format}/group/{name}`;

failure (network, deadline, 404, 5xx, off-origin redirect, unreadable reply) is
propagated and not cached (D23). Rejected: a bare sentinel (cannot say anonymous),
a result struct (interface churn). (2) The group cache file moves to an envelope
`version: 2` with `groups` and `refusals`; a refusal never overwrites a listing; a
listing clears the refusal. Legacy bare-map entries with no member are dropped
on read (CA6), entries with members kept. (3) Wording of the refusal lives in
`members_refused.go` (UX). No ADR: local, derived data, reversible (a revert reads
the v2 file as empty groups, `never`)."

## Risks and irreversible points

- **Irreversible (mild)**: the first write after the upgrade drops the legacy empty
  entries for good. Derived data; recovered by one `ctrl+r` per group.
- **Behaviour change visible to users**: a group that showed `0 · 3 days ago`
  after a swallowed 403 now shows `never` (CA6), then the refusal text after
  `ctrl+r`. Intended.
- **Pre-existing lost-update race** (not introduced, slightly widened): two
  concurrent discoveries for different groups each open their own
  `RegistryGroupCache`, `load` then `Set`; the last writer wins and can erase the
  other's write. `SetRefusal` is one more writer. Out of scope; candidate
  follow-up (single cache instance owned by the model, or re-read under a file
  lock before write).
- **Hypotheses to measure on the bench (NX-03, H2)**: a pull account gets 403 (not
  404 or an empty list) on the format endpoint; Nexus always sends `memberNames`
  for a group.
- **Security notes for the reviewer, out of scope**: `format` comes from the
  server and is put unescaped into the step-2 path (`nexus.go:158`), same origin
  only; `nexus.go:140` logs `type`/`format` with `%s` (D160 follow-up, `%q`).
  Either can be folded into step 1 if the reviewer wants it; neither is required
  by the criteria.

## Questions

**Q1 (needed before step 4, not before steps 1-3 and 5): should the refusal
survive the session?**
- (a) yes, persisted beside the listing (D2 option A): the Members column, the
  status line, MCP and optionally the browser header can say it after a restart.
  **Recommended**: CA6 already forces a cache format change, so the extra cost is
  one map, and without it the column says `never` after a restart, which is the
  "absence read as emptiness" family of defects this story fixes.
- (b) no, footer only (H1): drop `SetRefusal`, the `refusals` map, step 5 and H2–H4.
  Smaller, but CA4's "Registries tab / header" is then only a 3-second footer.
The UX proposal in progress decides much of this: if it places the text anywhere
but the footer, (a) is required.

- `fetchGroupMembers` (`nexus.go:154-188`) transforme toute erreur en « 0 membre » : 403, 5xx, échéance, réponse illisible et redirection hors origine.

**Décisions proposées**
- **Forme de l'erreur.** Un nouveau fichier `registrymgr/refusal.go` définit `ErrMembersRefused` et `*MembersRefusedError{Group, Status, Anonymous, Cause}`.
  - `Is` reconnaît la sentinelle et `Unwrap` rend le `*oci.StatusError` de NX-06.
  - Pourquoi ce choix : `errors.Is` et `errors.As` fonctionnent (CA1), et la règle D23 déjà présente dans la Cmd (`err == nil` ⇒ mise en cache) n'écrit plus le refus comme « 0 membre », sans autre changement.
  - Il sait aussi si la requête refusée était anonyme. Une simple sentinelle ne le peut pas, et une struct de résultat obligerait à changer l'interface `Detector` et une quarantaine de tests.
  - Seuls 401 et 403 comptent comme refus. Erreur réseau, échéance, 404, 5xx, redirection hors origine et réponse illisible donnent une erreur propagée, sans rien écrire dans le cache (CA3).
  - La relance anonyme de D156 ne change pas. Le premier essai décide, sauf si la relance réussit.
- **Le refus est stocké à côté de la liste, pas dedans.** Une table `refusals` est ajoutée près de `groups`.
  - Une entrée présente continue de vouloir dire « réponse réglée » pour tous les lecteurs : colonne Members, navigateur, MCP.

- **Cache en version 2 et CA6.** Le fichier `registry-groups.json` garde son nom et prend une enveloppe `{"version":2,"groups":…,"refusals":…}`, comme les autres caches du dépôt (`scan_file.go`, `image_scan.go`).
  - Un seul décodeur sert au cache et à la lecture seule du MCP.
  - Dans l'ancien format, les entrées qui ont des membres sont gardées : elles viennent forcément d'une lecture réussie.
  - Les entrées sans membre sont écartées et repassent à « never », sans migration manuelle.
  - La détection se fait sur `version >= 2`. Si l'on revient à une ancienne version, les groupes affichent « never », jamais un faux « 0 membre ».
- **Flux, Rule 110.** La Cmd fait le réseau et l'écriture disque, puis renvoie `RegistryGroupDetectedMsg{…, At}`. Seul le handler modifie `groupCache` et le nouveau `groupRefusals`. La conversion `refusalRecord(...)` est partagée entre disque et mémoire, et `msg.At` remplace le second `time.Now()`.

**Ce qui se passe aujourd'hui**
- `fetchGroupMembers` (`nexus.go:154-188`) transforme toute erreur en « 0 membre » : 403, 5xx, échéance, réponse illisible et redirection hors origine.
- `DetectGroup` (`:97-101`) rend alors `members, nil`.
- `detectRegistryGroupCmd` (`commands.go:513-516`) reçoit donc `err == nil` et écrase dans le cache les membres déjà connus par une liste vide.

**Décisions proposées**
- **Forme de l'erreur.** Un nouveau fichier `registrymgr/refusal.go` définit `ErrMembersRefused` et `*MembersRefusedError{Group, Status, Anonymous, Cause}`.
  - `Is` reconnaît la sentinelle et `Unwrap` rend le `*oci.StatusError` de NX-06.
  - Pourquoi ce choix : `errors.Is` et `errors.As` fonctionnent (CA1), et la règle D23 déjà présente dans la Cmd (`err == nil` ⇒ mise en cache) n'écrit plus le refus comme « 0 membre », sans autre changement.
  - Il sait aussi si la requête refusée était anonyme. Une simple sentinelle ne le peut pas, et une struct de résultat obligerait à changer l'interface `Detector` et une quarantaine de tests.
  - Seuls 401 et 403 comptent comme refus. Erreur réseau, échéance, 404, 5xx, redirection hors origine et réponse illisible donnent une erreur propagée, sans rien écrire dans le cache (CA3).
  - La relance anonyme de D156 ne change pas. Le premier essai décide, sauf si la relance réussit.
- **Le refus est stocké à côté de la liste, pas dedans.** Une table `refusals` est ajoutée près de `groups`.
  - Une entrée présente continue de vouloir dire « réponse réglée » pour tous les lecteurs : colonne Members, navigateur, MCP.
  - Un refus ne touche jamais aux membres connus (D23). Une liste réussie efface le refus.
- **Cache en version 2 et CA6.** Le fichier `registry-groups.json` garde son nom et prend une enveloppe `{"version":2,"groups":…,"refusals":…}`, comme les autres caches du dépôt (`scan_file.go`, `image_scan.go`).
  - Un seul décodeur sert au cache et à la lecture seule du MCP.
  - Dans l'ancien format, les entrées qui ont des membres sont gardées : elles viennent forcément d'une lecture réussie.
  - Les entrées sans membre sont écartées et repassent à « never », sans migration manuelle.
  - La détection se fait sur `version >= 2`. Si l'on revient à une ancienne version, les groupes affichent « never », jamais un faux « 0 membre ».
- **Flux, Rule 110.** La Cmd fait le réseau et l'écriture disque, puis renvoie `RegistryGroupDetectedMsg{…, At}`. Seul le handler modifie `groupCache` et le nouveau `groupRefusals`. La conversion `refusalRecord(...)` est partagée entre disque et mémoire, et `msg.At` remplace le second `time.Now()`.
- **Points d'accroche UI.** Tout le texte du refus vit dans un seul nouveau fichier, `members_refused.go`, sous forme de fonctions pures de `groupRefusalView{Refusal, Known, Declared}`. Le texte UX se branchera là.
